swap_risks: CRITICAL SUPPLY VOLTAGE RATING: LM358DR is limited to 30 V max (32 V abs max, p.4) whereas TL072IDR supports up to 40 V (42 V abs max, p.10). Installing a 5.5 V CMOS part on a 12 V–24 V rail causes instant breakdown.

CAUTION BANDWIDTH & PHASE MARGIN: GBWP differs by 7.5x (LM358DR: 0.7 MHz p.10 vs TL072IDR: 5.25 MHz p.15); higher-bandwidth replacements can oscillate with capacitive loads or stray feedback capacitance without an isolation resistor.
CAUTION SLEW RATE DIFFERENCE: Slew rate differs by 66.7x (LM358DR: 0.3 V/µs p.10 vs TL072IDR: 20 V/µs p.16); check full-power bandwidth SR / (2π·Vpeak).

HIGH INPUT BIAS CURRENT SHIFT: Typical Ib differs by 308x (LM358DR: 20000 pA p.10 vs TL072IDR: 65 pA p.15); high-impedance sensor dividers (>100 kΩ) suffer severe Ib·R DC offset error when swapping from CMOS/JFET to bipolar inputs.

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 4x (LM358DR: 350 µA/ch p.10 vs TL072IDR: 1400 µA/ch p.16); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH ABSOLUTE-MAX SURGE MARGIN: LM358DR has a lower Vs,abs,max rating (32 V, p.4) than TL072IDR (42 V, p.10); verify hot-plug, inductive kickback, and TVS clamp peaks stay safely below 32 V.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: TL072IDR requires Vs,min >= 4.5 V (p.11) vs 3 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.

HIGH TEMPERATURE GRADE MISMATCH: Rated ambient range differs (LM358DR: 0..70 °C Commercial (0°C to 70°C) vs TL072IDR: -40..85 °C Industrial (-40°C to 85°C)); LM358DR cold limit only 0 °C, LM358DR hot limit only 70 °C — verify product ambient qualification before swapping.
engineering_verdict: LM358DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and TL072IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because supply voltage Vs,max drops >=20%; GBWP differs 7.5x; slew rate differs 66.7x. Signal-chain deltas: GBWP 0.7 MHz (p.10) vs 5.25 MHz (p.15), supply ceiling 30 V (p.5) vs 40 V (p.11), Vos 7 mV (p.10) vs 6 mV (p.15), Ib 308x gap (20000 vs 65 pA), voltage noise 40 vs 37 nV/√Hz. Primary bench gotchas to watch: LM358DR "Non-Rail-to-Rail Upper Input and Output Headroom Ceiling" (p.10) and TL072IDR "Negative-Rail Input Headroom Limit and Legacy Phase Reversal Trap" (p.11). BOM decision: Choose LM358DR when ultra-low supply current (350 µA/ch) is prioritized; choose TL072IDR when supply rails exceed 30 V (rated up to 40 V) or closed-loop signal bandwidth requires 5.25 MHz GBWP. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.5) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
